correctness.rationale: A minimal dominating set in K_{m,n}, m,n>=2, is exactly one whole shore or one cross-shore two-set: any mixed larger set has a redundant vertex, while proper single-shore subset fails to dominate vertices on its own shore. The cross-shore signed sum factorizes into (m-2i)(n-2j), and full shores contribute the two parity signs. For odd-odd, product is odd, parity addition even => no zero. For even-even, product divisible by four, signs cancel only at i+j odd with one central Hamming weight; inclusion-exclusion yields the exact count. Even-odd, equal-sign case imposes product of absolute value two with a unique valid neighbor-center weight pair; opposite-sign case imposes central even-shore weight; binomial counts add. This proves all-parameter formulas. The trivial frequency maximizes absolute coefficient mn+2; parity plus near-center weight witnesses give sharp min |W|. I independently exhaustively summed binomial-weighted frequencies for all 576 parameter pairs 2<=m,n<=25, verifying zero formulas, gap 1/2 and max mn+2. Checks corroborate an elementary all-parameter proof, rather than extrapolate from finite sizes.
